questions.q: What triggered SO-48217's credit check hold in Chapter 2?
options: Harborview was a brand-new, unverified customer
The item was out of stock
The order's size, combined with Harborview's existing open balance
questions.explain: The order's value combined with Harborview's open balance failed the automatic credit check at submission.

questions.q: Why did SO-48217's first AutoInvoice run get rejected?
options: A new Harborview bill-to site had no remit-to address configured
The item did not exist in the price list
The ship date was in the past
questions.explain: A missing remit-to address on a newly created bill-to site caused the first AutoInvoice run to reject the line.

questions.q: What is Harborview's final open balance after the credit memo, before payment?
How many journal entries did SO-48217's full cycle generate, and from what events?
options: One entry, from the order submission only
Three entries: the invoice, the credit memo, and the cash receipt
Five entries, one for every lesson in Chapter 5
Zero — Order Management transactions have no accounting impact
questions.explain: Three distinct journal entries were generated: invoice, credit memo, and cash receipt application.

questions.q: What is the main lesson this recap is meant to leave you with?
options: Memorizing SO-48217's exact dollar figures for every future order
That every order always gets a credit hold
Recognizing the general shape of Order-to-Cash so you can apply it to orders with different numbers
That every shipment always has a return
questions.explain: The specific numbers belong to this fictional example; the goal is recognizing the repeatable shape of the O2C cycle.
